judge_assessment.explanation: The first hard failure is exact and I confirmed it item by item. Problem 6 prints "Two of the four terms disappear. Say in one sentence which ones and why" and verify.json id 6 is a lone `expand` check ((4x^3+x^2-6)-(4x^3-3x^2+2x-6) -> 4x^2-2x). Problem 10 prints "Explain in one sentence why squaring a binomial is not the same as squaring each term, then write the correct expansion" and id 10 is a lone `equiv`. Problem 11 prints "say in one sentence what the classmate left out" and id 11 is a lone `eval` at x=2. gate_log.txt ends "12 passed - 0 failed - 0 manual" and final_response.md states "Nothing is flagged manual", so three demanded explanations ship inside a claim of complete verification. The SECOND hard failure overstates. Problem 12's line "Multiply both products first, then subtract the second from the first" is a method hint under a single answer line; the one printed response is the final standard form, and verify id 12 checks exactly that ((x+2)(x^2-3x+5)-(x-1)(x+4) -> x^3-2x^2-4x+14, which I recomputed by hand). No intermediate product has its own answer slot, so nothing there is unverified that the sheet asks the student to hand in. The judge missed a cleaner instance of its own concern: problem 11 asks for the product in standard form AND its value at x=2, and only the value is checked - 3x^2+19x-14 appears nowhere in verify.json.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 11's trap is construction, not annotation: the classmate's reported -2 is DERIVED from the declared wrong method ("expr": "3*x*x-2*7") rather than typed into the stem, so the planted number cannot drift from the misconception it illustrates, and it reappears in the key's "Common wrong answers" block as "If they got -2: multiplied the first terms and the last terms only".

The difficulty ramp does real work without repeating a skeleton: problems 1-4 are one clean instance of each operation, 5 introduces missing degrees, 6 makes two of four terms cancel, 8 and 9 move to two variables where "like terms" gets its real test (3x^2y and xy are not like terms), and 12 multiplies a binomial by a trinomial before subtracting a second product.

The key's subtraction solutions always print the rewritten-as-addition line before collecting - "(7x^2-4x+1) + (-2x^2-6x+9)" - and the grading note names the exact wrong answer (5x^2+2x-8) that negating only the first term produces.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md line 257 already says it plainly - "Use `manual` for: graph sketches, sign charts, word problem setups, two-column proofs, constructions, ... and any explanation/reasoning answer" - but line 249 immediately narrows it ("Reserve `manual` for genuinely open reasoning") and tells the author to reframe error analysis "via the ordinary types". Read together, the guidance reads as a licence to type an explanation-bearing problem by its numeric half. Nothing in the gate chain notices, because no gate reads the problem prose looking for a demanded explanation.
evidence: worksheet problem 6: "Say in one sentence which ones and why" -- verify.json id 6 is a lone expand check
worksheet problem 10: "Explain in one sentence why squaring a binomial is not the same as squaring each term" -- id 10 is a lone equiv check
worksheet problem 11: "say in one sentence what the classmate left out" -- id 11 is a lone eval check

root_causes.description: SKILL.md's verification contract has a per-PROBLEM floor, not a per-RESPONSE-SLOT floor: "verification hard-fails unless every problem id 1..N has at least one check". A multi-part sheet therefore satisfies the gate with one scalar per id, and build.sh prints "0 manual" - which reads as "everything on this sheet was checked" rather than "every id had something checked". Problem 11 is the sharp case here: it demands the product in standard form and then its value at x=2, and only the value is verified.
evidence: worksheet problem 11: "Multiply (3x-2)(x+7) and write the product in standard form. Then evaluate your product at x = 2."
verify.json id 11: a single eval entry, expr "(3*x-2)*(x+7)", at x=2, expected 36 -- no expand check on 3*x**2+19*x-14
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers prints "11. 36" only, so a grader has no bank entry for the standard-form product

improvements.title: Explanations inside a computational problem need their own manual entry
improvements.proposed_change: Amend SKILL.md so a problem that demands prose alongside a computation is declared as TWO entries under one id: the ordinary typed check plus a `manual` entry whose `desc` states the full-credit reasoning. Back it with a lint in tests/check_layout.py that scans each problem's prose for "explain", "say in one sentence", "say what", "describe", "name the", and "why" used as a demand, and reports when that id carries no manual entry. Here it is three added entries: id 6 ("the x^3 terms and the constants cancel because they are identical and one is subtracted from the other"), id 10 ("names the two middle products that squaring term-by-term discards"), and id 11 ("the classmate omitted the outer and inner products"). All three descs already exist as prose in answer_key.pdf.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem 2 reads "Subtract, then say in one sentence which terms cancel and why" with a verify JSON holding only an expand entry for id 2. Assert the build reports problem 2 as manual (exit 2) instead of the current "0 manual" exit 0.
improvements.expected_impact: The three demanded explanations become honestly flagged, the manual count rises from 0 to 3, and the delivery text stops claiming "Nothing is flagged manual" for a sheet that asks for three written diagnoses.
improvements.risk: Medium: a verb lint over problem prose will fire on stems that use "explain" inside a hint rather than as a demand. Ship it as exit 2 (manual-review visibility), which is the honest outcome anyway and cannot block a correct build.

improvements.title: One verify entry per printed response slot, not per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: Change the coverage rule in SKILL.md from "every id 1..N has at least one check" to "every printed response slot has a check", and enforce it mechanically: add a slot counter to tests/check_layout.py (which already parses the worksheet .tex for answer-location macros) that counts, per problem, the lettered parts ((a)/(b)/(c)), the blank cells of a fill-in table, and each answer line, then reports when a problem's verify entries number fewer than its slots. Multi-entry ids are already legal and already used in these same files, so the fix adds entries, not machinery.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem 2 prints "(a) ... (b) ... (c) ..." with a verify JSON holding a single eval entry for id 2. Assert the gate chain flags problem 2 with the two uncovered parts named. Today the chain exits 0 and the delivery text claims full verification.
improvements.expected_impact: Multi-part problems stop being certified on the strength of their last line. Across this batch the same shape appears in curr-252, curr-256, curr-275, curr-276 and curr-300.
improvements.risk: Medium: counting slots from .tex will over-count where a lettered part is rhetorical rather than a response. Ship as exit 2 (manual visibility) before promoting to exit 1, so a correct build is never blocked by a parse artefact.

case_summary: Twelve mathematically clean polynomial problems - I re-expanded all twelve keyed results, including -12x^5+6x^3-15x^2, 4x^2-2x, 4x^2y-7y^2, 36 at x=2 and x^3-2x^2-4x+14 - on a genuine ramp with no repeated skeleton, and a key that shows the rewritten-as-addition line for every subtraction. It is rejected for a narrow, real reason: problems 6, 10 and 11 each demand a one-sentence written diagnosis, none is declared manual, and both the gate log and the delivery text advertise the sheet as fully machine-verified. The judge's second hard failure does not hold - problem 12 prints one answer slot and that slot is verified - but the judge missed a better example of the same concern: problem 11 asks for the standard-form product AND its value at x=2, and only the value is checked.
